headline: Govt hires law firm to seek Benazir Ahmed's return from UAE
summary: The Bangladesh government is taking legal steps to cancel the bail of former IGP Benazir Ahmed in Dubai to repatriate him.
details: The Bangladesh government has appointed a law firm to seek the cancellation of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed's bail in the UAE.
Home Minister Humaiun Kobir stated that the process to repatriate the former police chief from Dubai has officially begun.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid expressed optimism that Benazir Ahmed will be brought back to Bangladesh soon.
The move comes as the government aims to ensure the former IGP faces legal proceedings in Bangladesh following reports of his release from prison in Dubai.
caption:
The Bangladesh government is moving to bring back former IGP Benazir Ahmed from the UAE.

The Bangladesh government has appointed a law firm to seek the cancellation of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed's bail in the UAE.

Home Minister Humaiun Kobir stated that the process to repatriate the former police chief from Dubai has officially begun.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid expressed optimism that Benazir Ahmed will be brought back to Bangladesh soon.

The move comes as the government aims to ensure the former IGP faces legal proceedings in Bangladesh following reports of his release from prison in Dubai.

headline: MIST students win world championship in underwater robotics
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman pledges full government support for the world-champion MIST team and tech startups to boost Bangladesh's technological capabilities.
details: Students from the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST) have emerged as world champions in the MATE ROV 2026 International Underwater Robotic Drone Competition.
The team competed against 88 teams from 18 countries, including top universities and institutions from the USA, Canada, and China, beating the runner-up USA and third-place Canada.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with the champion team at the Prime Minister's Office on Sunday, congratulating them for bringing glory to Bangladesh on the international stage.
During the meeting, the students demonstrated their award-winning underwater robot to the Prime Minister, who discussed the robot's design, technical capabilities, and practical applications.
The Prime Minister assured the team of full government support for their future research, technical development, and the commercialization of their innovation.
He emphasized that young innovators are the future of Bangladesh and pledged that the government will support tech-driven startups through dedicated startup programs.
The Prime Minister also highlighted the government's goal to diversify the export economy by strengthening sectors like semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, furniture, and cosmetics.

He specifically noted that the semiconductor industry is being prioritized to attract foreign investment and develop a skilled workforce, calling on Bangladeshi semiconductor experts abroad to return home.
The meeting was attended by Defense Advisor Brigadier General (Retd.) A K M Shamsul Islam, MIST teachers, and members of the delegation.
caption:
From Bangladesh to the world! 🇧🇩 MIST students beat out 88 teams from 18 countries to become world champions in underwater robotics.

Students from the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST) have emerged as world champions in the MATE ROV 2026 International Underwater Robotic Drone Competition.

The team competed against 88 teams from 18 countries, including top universities and institutions from the USA, Canada, and China, beating the runner-up USA and third-place Canada.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with the champion team at the Prime Minister's Office on Sunday, congratulating them for bringing glory to Bangladesh on the international stage.

During the meeting, the students demonstrated their award-winning underwater robot to the Prime Minister, who discussed the robot's design, technical capabilities, and practical applications.

The Prime Minister assured the team of full government support for their future research, technical development, and the commercialization of their innovation.

He emphasized that young innovators are the future of Bangladesh and pledged that the government will support tech-driven startups through dedicated startup programs.

The Prime Minister also highlighted the government's goal to diversify the export economy by strengthening sectors like semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, furniture, and cosmetics.

He specifically noted that the semiconductor industry is being prioritized to attract foreign investment and develop a skilled workforce, calling on Bangladeshi semiconductor experts abroad to return home.

The meeting was attended by Defense Advisor Brigadier General (Retd.) A K M Shamsul Islam, MIST teachers, and members of the delegation.
